extracted_values_or_method: Bishenyi; Rwabayanga; Rusizi/Kamembe–Gihundwe; Rwandex–Magerwa.
interpretation_or_caveat: Names vary across report sections and tables (e.g., Rusizi versus Kamembe–Gihundwe; Magerwa versus Rwandex–Magerwa). Resolve study polygons before comparing site values.

extracted_values_or_method: 3-D visual interpretation of Google Earth imagery; spatial resolution 30–60 cm; image captures 2000–2021; imagery credited to DigitalGlobe or CNES/Airbus; analysis alongside field photographs.
interpretation_or_caveat: This is the local Step 1 imagery statement. It does not document the exact image dates/intervals for each of the regional 2,544 shallow points.

extracted_values_or_method: Shallow landslides defined as estimated depth <5 m; relative depth estimated visually from scarp and deposit shape/size. Recent failures are between two image dates; old failures are present in the oldest image without visible activity.
interpretation_or_caveat: Depth is visually estimated, not measured per point. Image-bracket dating is interval-censored, not an exact occurrence date.

extracted_values_or_method: 22 old deep-seated landslides and 5 recent deep-seated flow slides/earthflows in four sub-catchments; features manually assigned polygons.
interpretation_or_caveat: Old ages are undetermined; some may be thousands of years old. Recent events are bounded by image acquisitions, not necessarily dated to a day.

extracted_values_or_method: No shallow landslide features were identified in satellite imagery in the four local catchments over the preceding ~20 years; authors say this does not prove none occurred. Lake Kivu intense convective events can produce clusters of hundreds to thousands of slope failures over a few (tenths of) km².
interpretation_or_caveat: Small scars can be missed or obscured by weathering, erosion, vegetation regrowth and human activity. Non-detection is not a negative sample.

extracted_values_or_method: Creep-affected hillslopes and gullies are explicitly described as non-comprehensive; small road-related failures may be too small to identify in Google Earth.
interpretation_or_caveat: This further demonstrates detection and process-specific incompleteness.

extracted_values_or_method: Report states local Step 1 inventory is much too limited for data-driven susceptibility/hazard models across the four small catchments. It uses a broader western-Rwanda shallow-landslide inventory for regional susceptibility and hazard.
interpretation_or_caveat: The two inventories have distinct roles: local deep-seated/ground-deformation susceptibility versus regional shallow-initiation susceptibility/hazard. The “in review” 2022 citation was later published; see source crosswalk.

topic: Regional shallow initiation inventory and timing
extracted_values_or_method: 2,544 recent shallow landslide observations, identified by visual Google Earth analysis over 2000–2019; each slide represented by one manually defined initiation point/pixel. Failure timing is said to fall between two satellite-image dates.
interpretation_or_caveat: No daily occurrence dates or image-date pair table is printed in the report. The 2,544 count is points/slides, not independent rainfall-triggering days.

extracted_values_or_method: Average mapped total landslide area 725 m²: source area 121 m² and impact area 604 m². Impact area was excluded from the susceptibility response; the initiation/source area was represented by one point.
interpretation_or_caveat: A point labels the initiation/source location, not the whole affected footprint. In §2.5.2 the report assumes 5 m² of impact area per 1 m² of initiation area.

extracted_values_or_method: Figure shows 2,544 shallow landslide locations, 83 non-stationary knickpoints used to delineate rejuvenated versus relict landscapes, two clusters associated with intense convective rainfall events, and examples of total-area versus source-area mapping.
interpretation_or_caveat: The plotted points are an inventory for relative susceptibility/hazard; exact event-date pairs and source polygons are not included in the PDF.

extracted_values_or_method: Elevation, slope, profile/planar curvature, north/east exposure (DEM 10/30 m); rejuvenated landscape (1:1,000); distance to rivers (10/30 m); lithology and distance to faults (10/30 m); peak ground acceleration (PGA, 2.2 km); land use/cover; road presence within 50 m; clay content (>35% clay). Land cover has six classes; lithology five classes. Sources include Rwanda DEM/SRTM, Depicker et al., Smets/Delvaux, GGGI/RWB and RTDA.
interpretation_or_caveat: The final model selection is the 30 m model without lithology. Table 1 mixes predictor-native scales; this is not a single uniform raster resolution.

extracted_values_or_method: 2,544 initiation observations plus an equal number of randomly selected non-landslide/background points across the landscape outside landslide areas; forward stepwise logistic regression; random 10-fold cross-validation.
interpretation_or_caveat: The background points are sampled pseudo-absences, not verified non-events. Report does not show spatial blocking, temporal holdout, independent external test, storm grouping, or prospective verification.

extracted_values_or_method: 10 m DEM: 89.3% with lithology and 85.0% without lithology. 30 m DEM: 91.1% with lithology and 88.8% without lithology. Report selects 30 m without lithology because lithology is coarse at the watershed scale and performance difference is called marginal.
interpretation_or_caveat: AUC is discrimination between the mapped positive points and the chosen random background sample; not calibrated probability, warning skill, or independent spatial/temporal generalization.

extracted_values_or_method: Importance is assessed by univariate susceptibility-model AUC. Figure labels: slope 88.9%; elevation 63.1%; distance to faults 60.0%; distance to rivers 59.0%; planar curvature 58.4%; land cover 55.2%; PGA 54.1%; road presence 53.5%; east exposure 53.0%; rejuvenated landscape 52.9%; clay content 51.1%; north exposure 50.4%. Profile curvature has no legible labelled score.
interpretation_or_caveat: These are univariate AUCs, not permutation importance or coefficient effects from the final multivariable model. The report says roads may be underrepresented because very small road failures were not mapped and DEMs do not encode engineered cuts.

extracted_values_or_method: For continuous predictors derived from the 10 m DEM, reported VIFs: slope 1.04; elevation 1.73; profile curvature 1.17; planar curvature 1.20; north/east exposure 1.00 each; PGA 2.96; distance to rivers 1.16; distance to faults 3.46; road buffer 1.00; >35% clay 1.06. Authors use VIF >4 as problematic and report none.
interpretation_or_caveat: This checks collinearity among continuous predictors, not spatial independence, sample bias, calibration, or generalization.

extracted_values_or_method: Condition-index thresholds: CI >30 signals moderate-to-strong multicollinearity; CI <10 indicates weak multicollinearity. Authors report no problematic multicollinearity.
interpretation_or_caveat: Another predictor-correlation diagnostic only; it does not validate random cross-validation or the occurrence sample.

extracted_values_or_method: Susceptibility is divided into classes; for each class the total affected area of shallow landslide sources during the ~20-year observation period is averaged annually and normalized per km², producing m²/year/km².
interpretation_or_caveat: This is a retrospective area-rate by static susceptibility class, not a rainfall-trigger model or point-specific failure probability.

extracted_values_or_method: Figure 6 depicts increasing affected area with susceptibility; text gives approximate rate ~400 m²/year/km² for susceptibility 0.9–1.0 and ~150 for 0.8–0.9. Figure 7 compares susceptibility distributions and rate-weighted distributions by catchment; text says Rwandex–Magerwa has the highest average hazard and Rwabayanga the lowest.
interpretation_or_caveat: Approximate curve readings should not replace the discrete Table 6 values. Figures are based on the same retrospective mapped inventory and do not provide independent temporal validation.

extracted_values_or_method: Susceptibility classes and average rates: 0–10% (highest susceptibility) = 365; >10–30% = 90; >30–60% = 18; >60–100% = 1 m²/year/km². Figure 8 panels: Bishenyi, Rusizi, Rwabayanga, Rwandex–Magerwa.
interpretation_or_caveat: Rates apply to shallow landslide initiation/source area only; they are class-level annualized historical area rates.

extracted_values_or_method: Report interprets 365 m²/year/km² in the top susceptibility class as 365 m² source area/year per 1 km²; says “~2700 years” for a pixel, assumes 5 m² impact per 1 m² initiation, estimates 6×365 m² impact/year = 0.2%, then asserts about 1% after underestimation. Table 7 area (km²; % of site): rate 1—Bishenyi 21.06/44.6, Rwabayanga 5.34/68.3, Rusizi 15.98/75.9, Rwandex–Magerwa 6.77/69.7; rate 18—19.54/41.3, 1.84/23.5, 4.40/20.9, 2.19/22.5; rate 90—5.96/12.6, 0.59/7.5, 0.66/3.1, 0.68/7.0; rate 365—0.71/1.5, 0.05/0.6, 0.02/0.1, 0.08/0.8.
interpretation_or_caveat: ~2700 years is a reciprocal area-rate analogy, not an empirically estimated per-pixel return period. The 0.2% estimate is arithmetic from assumed source-to-impact scaling; the 1% correction is qualitative and no detection-correction factor is measured.

extracted_values_or_method: Desktop spatial overlap of hazard-rate zonation and land-use categories for current 2018 situation and projected 2050 master plan. Report says no vulnerability databases were received.
interpretation_or_caveat: Exposure is not vulnerability or risk. No damage functions, building fragility, population/time-of-day, or social coping-capacity data are reported.

extracted_values_or_method: Catchment Restoration Opportunity Mapping Support System uses RUSLE to estimate sheet/rill water erosion; report says it does not model gullying or landslides. It warns erosion controls that reduce runoff can raise infiltration/regolith water content and create more landslide-favorable conditions.
interpretation_or_caveat: CROM DSS is not a landslide forecast or a standalone basis for terrace/drainage design; site-specific hydrology/geotechnical review is needed.

extracted_values_or_method: No specific field measurements; mitigation choices and costs are assumption-based. Focus is rates 365 and 90 m²/year/km². Table 15 area under those two classes (ha): Bishenyi 666.7 of total 4,686.8; Rwabayanga 68.4 of 809.0; Rwandex–Magerwa 63.9 of 979.3; Kamembe–Gihundwe 76.3 of 2,123.6. Assumptions include 30% reforestation coverage and 500 m drainage trenches/ditches per 3 ha.
interpretation_or_caveat: These are planning assumptions and cost estimates, not field-validated interventions. The report says it excludes measures expected to increase infiltration.

extracted_values_or_method: Bishenyi: agroforestry + progressive terraces, reforestation, trenches/ditches; coverage 466.69 ha, 200.01 ha, 111.10 km. Rwabayanga: same plus gully rehabilitation; 47.88 ha, 20.52 ha, 11.40 km, 1.50 ha gully rehabilitation. Kamembe–Gihundwe: agroforestry + progressive terraces, reforestation, trenches/ditches; 53.41 ha, 22.89 ha, 12.70 km. Rwandex–Magerwa: reforestation and trenches/ditches; 44.73 ha and 10.60 km.
interpretation_or_caveat: The Bill of Quantities table shows unit-cost and total-cost columns, but the extracted report page does not provide filled cost values. These are proposed measures, not tested results.
